section_summary: This section contains translated transcripts of Japanese shortwave broadcasts from July 1941, including news, commentary, music listings, and talks addressed to Japanese residents overseas. The broadcasts promote Japan’s war in China, discuss the German–Soviet war and Anglo–Soviet agreement, and report on Japanese politics and domestic affairs. A Federal Bureau of Investigation cover letter transmits later transcripts to the State Department; pages 34–40 repeat the July 16 transcript on pages 24–30.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 program transcript, concluding pages
subfiles.about: News and an army publicity official’s talk mark the fourth anniversary of the war in China.
subfiles.summary: The surviving pages list international and Japanese news, then summarize Masao’s speech defending Japan’s campaign in China and denouncing aid to Chiang Kai-shek.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 program, July 8
subfiles.about: Commentary presents Japan’s war in China as the foundation of a new order in East Asia.
subfiles.summary: Recorded final half hour of commentary and the national anthem.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 program, July 9
subfiles.about: The program combines domestic news with Giichi Okamura’s anniversary address on Japan’s war and foreign policy.
subfiles.summary: After provincial news, Okamura discusses the German–Soviet war, the Axis, Japan’s military campaign in China, recognition of the Nanjing government, and Dutch East Indies trade talks. He urges overseas Japanese listeners to reject reports of hardship in Japan.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 program, July 10
subfiles.about: Noboru Imao addresses Japanese residents in America on world events and their conduct abroad.
subfiles.summary: Imao predicts deeper American involvement in the European war, praises Japan’s resolve, and asks overseas Japanese to consider how their actions affect relations with America.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 program, July 11
subfiles.about: Commentary, regional news, and a talk describe international tensions and Osaka Harbor.
subfiles.summary: The transcript covers American policy in East Asia, provincial reports, and Yoshinori Miyauchi’s account of Osaka Harbor’s development.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 program, July 12
subfiles.about: A children’s broadcast discusses summer activities, the Kanmon Tunnel, and Hitler.
subfiles.summary: The speaker describes Japanese children’s wartime summer activities, celebrates construction of the undersea rail tunnel, and offers admiring remarks about Hitler.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 program, July 13
subfiles.about: A partial recording discusses Soviet strategy and German advances.
subfiles.summary: The commentator weighs reported Soviet losses and prospects for continued resistance.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 program, July 14
subfiles.about: News reports cover the German–Soviet war, the Anglo–Soviet agreement, and Japanese affairs.
subfiles.summary: The broadcast reports military claims from Europe, views of the Anglo–Soviet agreement, Japanese domestic news, and the completed Kanmon Tunnel.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 program, July 15
subfiles.about: The broadcast reports war news and argues that British agreements with Soviet Russia and Chongqing threaten Japan.
subfiles.summary: News items describe the German advance, newspaper reactions to the Anglo–Soviet agreement, Japanese operations in China, and political meetings in Japan. Extended commentary portrays British cooperation with Soviet Russia and Chongqing as unstable and hostile to Japan’s plans in East Asia. Aritsune Sugimoto then speaks about conditions in Canton.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal of Tokyo broadcast transcripts
subfiles.about: Hoover sends translated Tokyo broadcast transcripts for July 16–23, 1941.
subfiles.summary: FBI cover letter transmitting enclosed broadcasts to the State Department.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 program, July 16
subfiles.about: News and commentary address the German–Soviet war, the Anglo–Soviet agreement, and Japan’s position in East Asia.
subfiles.summary: The transcript reports Japanese personnel movements, conditions in Chongqing, and competing claims from the German–Soviet front. Lengthy commentary draws on Japanese newspaper editorials to argue that British and Soviet cooperation is weak and potentially harmful to Japan. Hidejirō Nagata urges overseas Japanese to trust Japan’s strength and determination.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 program, July 17
subfiles.about: The broadcast reports the Konoe cabinet’s resignation, American defense measures, and war news.
subfiles.summary: News covers selection of Japan’s next premier, American military and diplomatic measures, German operations, and Japanese activity in China. Commentary praises cooperation between Japan and the Nanjing government.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Station JLU4 program, July 16
subfiles.about: These pages repeat the July 16 transcript on pages 24–30.
subfiles.summary: The repeated copy contains war news, commentary on the Anglo–Soviet agreement, provincial reports, and Hidejirō Nagata’s address to overseas Japanese.

subfiles.title: Station JLU4 program, July 18
subfiles.about: The broadcast reports Konoe’s appointment to form a cabinet, war developments, and Japanese domestic news.
subfiles.summary: News includes Konoe’s renewed appointment, Japanese military and shipping movements, Axis activities, and the German–Soviet front. Commentary reviews the former cabinet; regional reports and a talk on Japanese dancing close the program.
